full_judgment: But even before insertion of the said provision the highest Court of this country granted anticipatory bail to a person appearing before it when such ,person could satisfy the Court that he was being threatened with arrest by the police to unnecessarily harass and humiliate him out of malafide motive or without rhyme or reason. The earliest case decided by the then Federal Court of Pakistan in this respect is the case of Crown vs. Khushi Mohammad reported in 5 DLR (FC) 143. In that case anticipatory bail granted by the High Court Court was set aside by the Federal Court taking the view that unless a person is in custody or some sort of restraint, he cannot be released on bail. In the case of Ghulam Haider vs. Karim Baksh, reported in 15 DLR (SC) 2 anticipatory bail was refused to the petitioners on the ground that offence under section 326 of the Penal Code with which they were accused of was punishable with imprisonment for life.
